Symptoms began or became problematic after retirement (change in evening activities), causing social/marital impairment. Objective testing supports a phase-advanced circadian rhythm: actigraphy shows consistently early sleep onset and wake times over two weeks; polysomnography shows normal sleep efficiency but with advanced timing; melatonin secretion is increased in the early evening, indicating an early circadian phase. There is no evidence of other sleep disorders (PSG normal), no significant medical, psychiatric, or substance causes, and behavioral attempts (caffeine) have not shifted the timing. These features meet criteria for a circadian rhythm sleep-wake disorder of the advanced sleep-wake phase type (advanced sleep phase disorder).

DIAGNOSIS: Circadian rhythm sleep-wake disorder, advanced sleep-wake phase type (advanced sleep phase disorder).
